tasks.title: HANGS Construction · FY2026 Cash Audit
tasks.description: Audit HANGS Construction Development LP's cash at June 30, 2026 from 10 Excel and PDF files: the client's books and its bank reconciliation, the confirmation the audit team sent, the bank's two answers and the escrow company's report, sent to the audit team directly, and the June and July bank statements. Agree the confirmed balance to the reconciliation and the trial balance, trace every outstanding item to July, age the old check, search for the bank's charge, test the cut-off and look for restricted cash. Produce formula-linked workpapers with tickmarks and a draft findings memo. The CPA reviews, decides every open item and concludes; the machine gives no opinion.
tasks.outputs: Two files: formula-linked Excel workpapers with tickmarks and evidence tabs, and a draft cash audit findings memo PDF for the CPA with evidence trails and the original files attached
tasks.gates: Draft workpapers and findings, not reviewed, concluded or signed. Not an audit report and no opinion. Open items stay open. The CPA concludes.
tasks.periodLine: FY2026: cash at June 30, 2026 · bank confirmation and reconciliation testing for the CPA.

lines.text: $239,760.00 to HANGS Property Holdings LLC and $240.00 to HANGS General Partner Inc left by wire on June 30, 2026 and are in the books that day; together $240,000.00, the distributions in the trial balance. There are no transfers to test: one account at the bank, one cash account in the books. The 3 other July payments are not in the June books. lines.text: The bank reports no holds, liens, pledges, set-off or compensating balance, and no loans whose terms could restrict cash. The escrow company wired all 104 closings in full, $3,276,000.00, so nothing is held back for the seller. The statements show one cash line, $29,900.00, all of total assets. No restricted cash, so the statements need no restricted cash disclosure; the CPA decides.

lines.text: Ready for the CPA
Add up what was found and set it against materiality

Known misstatements add up to $700.00, 5.8% of the $12,000.00 materiality and under performance materiality of $9,000.00: the unrecorded bank charge (FEE-01). Proposed: debit a bank charges expense, credit cash. If the client declines, it goes on the summary of passed adjustments. Voiding stale check 1043 would put $700.00 back in cash against the warranty liability (STALE-01), so the two together leave cash at $29,900.00. Concluding is the CPA's job; the machine stops here.
